study type: Repeated cross-sectional analysis with interrupted time series
cohort: The study included 843,133 low-risk nulliparous individuals in the US delivering a non-anomalous, cephalic, singleton infant, excluding those with hypertension, diabetes, or small-for-gestational age infants.
finding: Dissemination of the ARRIVE trial was associated with an increase in the rate of induction at 40 weeks among patients who remained pregnant after 39 weeks.
mod_finding: Despite the increase in 40-week inductions, there was no population-level decrease in cesarean delivery rates, suggesting the benefits of induction may not extrapolate to this cohort.
gest_age: 40 weeks gestation (for induction of labor among patients remaining pregnant after 39 weeks)
